name: Mission of Burma
label: Matador
lede: Four years, one EP, one album, and a guitarist whose ears gave out; then, nineteen years later, the Boston band everyone had been covering came back and made four more records as loud as the first.

eras.title: Sun Ra until the drummer walks out
eras.text: Out of the ashes of a band called Moving Parts, Roger Miller and Clint Conley built a four-piece where the fourth member played tape machines instead of an instrument. Boston college radio got it before anyone else did.

years.h: Roger Miller and Clint Conley audition drummers the hard way
years.p: After Moving Parts splits amicably, Roger Miller and Clint Conley play 'out' music like Sun Ra and James Brown at drummer auditions until each applicant gives up and leaves.
years.xp: Conley took the name from a plaque he saw on a diplomatic building in New York reading Mission of Burma. He liked that it sounded murky and disturbing.

q: crossing John Coltrane with the Ramones
years.h: First show: a trio at Boston's Modern Theater
years.p: With ex-Molls drummer [[Peter Prescott|f69ea4d3-4065-49ff-b076-585bfc6e79ff]], Mission of Burma debuts as a trio at the Modern Theater. Their sets were built by committee minutes before going on stage.
years.xp: Prescott's own description of the band: experimentation plus primal fury. Boston critic Tristram Lozaw said the shows swung between spectacular and a ball of incomprehensible noise, and nobody knew which they'd get.

years.h: Martin Swope joins to play the tape machines
years.p: Roger Miller writes Nu Disco and calls Martin Swope for tape loops. Swope runs the live sound and feeds sped-up, slowed and reversed tape of the band back through the PA.

years.h: Peking Spring is WMBR's most-played song of 1979
years.p: MIT station WMBR spins Clint Conley's Peking Spring so hard it tops the station's year. By the time a label turned up, the band felt the song had run its course.

years.h: Academy Fight Song / Max Ernst · Ace of Hearts
years.p: The first single pairs Clint Conley's Academy Fight Song with Roger Miller's Max Ernst. The band hated Rick Harte's clean production; the first pressing sold out fast anyway.
years.xp: [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] and Miracle Legion later covered Academy Fight Song.

eras.title: Too loud to last
eras.text: Mission of Burma made one EP and one album for Boston's Ace of Hearts, both now counted among the great American records of the decade. Its volume was the point, and it cost Miller his hearing.

years.h: Signals, Calls, and Marches sells out 10,000 copies
years.p: Recorded January to March 1981 with Rick Harte producing, the EP opens with Clint Conley's That's When I Reach for My Revolver. The 10,000 first pressing is gone by year's end.
years.xp:
Revolver went on to be covered by [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]], [[Graham Coxon|fb56cc34-2ab1-4621-ac18-9bf2895e5f4f]], [[Catherine Wheel|37e3dd97-73f9-4c69-b50d-0c0e3c47c40c]], [[Pegboy|13e78eec-9ee4-47f2-a50e-2a9f519cb6e2]] and [[Down by Law|7d990fa3-e1a0-4d6e-b266-222a66bd3f83]], among others.

Roger Miller remembered a Cleveland show around 1981 or 1982 where fans who loved the record backed against the wall at the live volume and wouldn't clap.
play: That's When I Reach for My Revolver

years.h: Mission of Burma backs Dredd Foole as the Din
years.p: Singer Dan Ireton records a two-song single with the band as Dredd Foole and the Din: Roger Miller on organ, Clint Conley on lead guitar, Martin Swope on prepared bass.

years.h: Vs., recorded at Normandy Sound, Rhode Island
years.p: Mission of Burma's only 1980s album, made January to April 1982 with Rick Harte. The Boston Phoenix said Trem Two sounded like the universe being born and destroyed.
years.xp: Robert Christgau gave it a B+ in the Village Voice and later said he should have given it an A−. The band [[Versus|ee7db106-6996-42a9-981d-b2d55a9b8366]] named itself after the album.

years.h: Roger Miller's tinnitus breaks up Mission of Burma
years.p: Roger Miller's tinnitus from years of extreme volume reaches a dangerous level. On the farewell tour he plays in rifle-range earmuffs over foam earplugs.
years.xp: The last shows went through Boston, including the Bradford Hotel and the Channel, plus Chicago, New York and Detroit. They were taped, and became The Horrible Truth About Burma, with covers of [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]]' 1970 and [[Pere Ubu|5a54b72e-bfb3-4ca6-944a-e17261399965]]'s Heart of Darkness.

eras.title: Nineteen years of being covered
eras.text: The members scattered into tape-loop art music, new punk bands and a TV newsroom. Meanwhile the records got reissued, the songs got covered, and a generation of bands learned them.

years.h: The Horrible Truth About Burma, the farewell tour live
years.p: Ace of Hearts releases the 1983 farewell tour recordings. The title is an inside joke about how chaotic Mission of Burma's shows could be.

years.h: Birdsongs of the Mesozoic and Volcano Suns carry on
years.p: Roger Miller and Martin Swope work in [[Birdsongs of the Mesozoic|0a3d592f-8848-4ac0-888d-f31eb4be5bfe]] with Erik Lindgren. Peter Prescott forms [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]], later Kustomized and the Peer Group.

years.h: Clint Conley produces Yo La Tengo's first album
years.p: Clint Conley produces [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]]'s Ride the Tiger, then gets a broadcast journalism master's and works as a producer on WCVB-TV's Chronicle for years.

years.h: Rykodisc's Mission of Burma CD breaks the 80-minute mark
years.p: Rykodisc's compilation Mission of Burma is the first CD to run past 80 minutes, over the format's supposed limit.

years.h: Our Band Could Be Your Life gives Burma a chapter
years.p: Michael Azerrad's book names Mission of Burma among 13 bands that built the American underground. Clint Conley starts playing again with his new band, Consonant.

eras.title: Two shows turn into forever
eras.text: Conley's return to playing opened the door. Swope was gone, so a friend from Prescott's old band took over the tapes, and a pair of reunion dates became a second career.

q: Bob opted for maintaining the original integrity, and uses a tape deck.
years.h: Mission of Burma reunites, with Bob Weston on tape
years.p: One Boston show and one New York show sell out so fast they become three nights and two. Martin Swope, now in Hawaii, declines; [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s Bob Weston takes over.
years.xp: Weston had played in Prescott's [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]]. Miller told him he could use digital gear; Weston stuck with reel-to-reel. He later added an Electro-Harmonix looper live but kept real tape in the studio.

eras.title: The Matador years
eras.text: Most reunions coast. Mission of Burma made new albums on Matador Records that critics put next to the old ones, got its catalog reissued, and got a day named after it.

years.h: ONoffON, the first new record in 19 years
years.p: Mission of Burma's Matador debut, produced by Bob Weston with Rick Harte, finishes 90th in the Village Voice Pazz & Jop poll.

years.h: The Obliterati, once called Aluminum Washcloth
years.p: Pitchfork ranks it the 33rd best record of 2006. The documentary Not a Photograph: The Mission of Burma Story comes out the same year.

years.h: Matador reissues Signals, Vs. and Horrible Truth
years.p: Remastered editions of all three 1980s records; Signals, Calls, and Marches gains two unreleased songs from its first session.

years.h: Peter Prescott gives Mission of Burma a couple more years
years.p: Peter Prescott tells L.A. Record that the physical demands of Burma shows limit the band to a couple more years at most.

years.h: Boston declares Mission of Burma Day
years.p: The Boston City Council's proclamation is marked at a ceremony at MIT in Cambridge, home of WMBR, the station that played Peking Spring to death in 1979.

years.h: The Sound the Speed the Light · Matador
years.p: Fourteen songs, preceded in August by a Matador 7-inch of two non-album tracks.

eras.title: Good friends, finally quiet
eras.text: One more album on a new label, a last show in Berlin, then an amicable end. The only returns since have been for a cause.

years.h: Unsound on Fire Records, after Matador
years.p: Mission of Burma parts ways with Matador and makes its fifth album for Fire Records, led by the single Dust Devil.

years.h: Mission of Burma's last live show is in Berlin
years.p: The band plays Berlin in 2016. It turns out to be the final gig of the reunion era.

years.h: WBUR reports Mission of Burma has disbanded
years.p: A 2019 Facebook post had said no more albums; in June 2020 WBUR reports the split is amicable and the members remain good friends.

years.h: One-off benefit for Jeff Conolly of the Lyres
years.p: Mission of Burma plays the Middle East Downstairs in Cambridge for [[Lyres|f15227ba-75e0-490c-a817-63bf8f54fee7]] leader Jeff Conolly, Clint Conley's high school friend from Darien. Another benefit follows at Brighton Music Hall on August 14.
